You were right that it's small, but it wasn't quite what the title said. The description field already exists everywhere — you can type one and it saves fine. It just never gets read. Two reasons, and your mid-flight note caught the second one:

The event page reads the *date's* description and never looks up at the series it came from. Location already does look up; description was missed. So a description on the Midweek Gathering series is invisible on every date of it.

And there's no way to write one for a single date, because the edit panel is switched off for anything recurring. That's the bit you asked for.

One thing worth knowing, because it's the only real risk here. Most dates of a repeating event have no record in the database at all — they're worked out from the pattern on the fly. Writing a description to one *creates* that record, and the save code doesn't currently attach the "who can see this" marker. Without it, the date goes invisible to everyone, including the person who just typed. That exact bug bit this codebase once before, on rosters, and there's a comment in the file about it. ## Where it stands

CONTEXT.md exists and I read it in full, plus ADR-0018. The MS-288 change adds `descriptionOf` (mirroring the existing `locationOf`) to `events-occurrence-core.js` (and its `functions/shared` twin), a per-date "description" box on `calendar-event.html`, and extends `saveOccurrenceDetails` in `events-store.js` so a description-only edit on a bare date of a series creates that occurrence document.

**The visibility-stamping code (ADR-0018) is correct.** `events-store.js` (`saveOccurrenceDetails`, ~lines 950–990) stamps a newly-created occurrence with the series' `visibility`/`rosterShared` via `stampFor`, leaves an existing document's stamp alone, and writes `seriesId`/`date` so the two-query visibility read in ADR-0018 §5 still finds it. `test/events-store.test.js` (~1757–1791) covers exactly this, including the Sunday-Service-is-always-public case. No contradiction with the ADR.

**The real finding is a model/code conflict, not a bug.** CONTEXT.md states, as an explicit architectural line under **Event occurrence**:

> "**One date decides WHO; the Event decides WHAT.** ... Which Roles an Event carries, who may see it, and what colour it draws are true of every date, so they are set once in [[Event series management]]."
(`CONTEXT.md` ~line 549-552)

and under **Event series management**:

> "everything true of every date: its name, start time, place, **description**, recurrence pattern, [[Event visibility]], colour" (`CONTEXT.md` ~line 570-571)

MS-288 gives one date a description that can differ from, and override, the series' — a genuine per-date "WHAT," not a "WHO." The code is fully aware it's doing something new here and argues for it at length:

> "unlike a place it is expected to differ: 'bring the trestle tables, we're eating after' is true of one week and wrong for the rest." (`public/events-occurrence-core.js` ~line 443-445, mirrored in `functions/shared/events-occurrence-core.js`)

and the UI panel is titled accordingly:

> "Just this date ... Anything true of every one of these belongs on the event itself." (`public/calendar-event.html` ~line 598-603)

`calendar-event.js`'s `occurrenceOwnFields` getter (~1591-1595) enforces the same split in code: a series date owns only `['description']`; everything else (`name`, `date`, `endDate`, `time`, `location`) stays event-only, one-offs excepted. So the code carves out exactly one exception to "the Event decides WHAT," and CONTEXT.md's two passages above still state the rule without that exception. This is worth a human call: either CONTEXT.md's "everything true of every date" line needs a carve-out for description, or the feature needs to be reconsidered against a model that was deliberately drawn that way. I'm not picking a side — just flagging that the two currently disagree, in the exact section the ticket touches.

**The stale line is confirmed.** CONTEXT.md ~line 571 says Event series management is "Reached at `calendar-event.html?series=<id>`." But `public/calendar-event.js` (lines 48, 308, 392, 787) now redirects there to `recurring-events.html?series=<id>`, and `public/recurring-events.js` itself narrates the move in comments: "to be a second page at `calendar-event.html?series=…`" (line 12) and "so `calendar-event.html?series=` is not a page any [more]" (line 878, MS-229 cited explicitly). CONTEXT.md was not updated by MS-288 even though this diff edits `calendar-event.js`/`calendar-event.html` directly — the exact files whose own comments record that the URL in CONTEXT.md is dead. It would have cost nothing to fix while in there, but it's a pre-existing staleness, not something MS-288 introduced.

The feature works as you asked. A description on a repeating event now shows on every date of it, and each date has its own box for what's different that week. Empty box, and the date just says what the event says.

Three things worth telling you.

The reviewers caught real problems, not nitpicks. The most useful: writing a note on a date that had no record yet creates one, and the code wasn't attaching the "who can see this" marker — the note would have landed in the database and gone invisible to everyone, including whoever typed it. There's now a test that writes a note and then reads it back as an ordinary member, which is the only test that actually proves it. Two smaller ones too: typing spaces into an empty box would have written a whole record to store nothing, and a half-loaded page briefly thought it was a repeating event.

The bigger one is a disagreement between the code and your model. `CONTEXT.md` says "one date decides who, the event decides what" — and this feature is the first exception to it. Rather than let them quietly disagree, I wrote the exception into `CONTEXT.md` with the reasoning, and while there also stated the read-through rule the model was leaning on without ever saying. If you'd rather the rule stayed clean and the feature bent instead, that's your call to reverse — but I'd keep it. A description is genuinely the one fact about an event that can differ week to week.

I also tidied something adjacent. There were three places in the code that create an event date, each carrying its own copy of the same safety warning, remembered separately. They now share one helper, so the next person to write one doesn't have to know. Behaviour is identical at the two old sites.
